# Rule C2: Outlaw Rules
Being an antagonist does not allow you to stop playing a character. Whilst engaging in this activity, you should seek to make shifts more engaging and fun, as you will be an initiator of ‘drama’ and ‘disequilibrium’ in a round.
Success as an Outlaw is not measured in financial or combat, [bold]but in aiding in telling the most interesting story for everyone[/bold].
- [bold]Outlaws set their own objectives[/bold]. They are allowed to engage and disengage with Outlaw Bounties and Jobs as they see fit, and can perform damage and activities to achieve their own goals. -- Damage must be minimal and proportional, although through roleplay damage becomes more proportional. [italic](Example: Holding a gun to someone's face as a hostage to get everyone to pay you is acceptable, shooting everyone dead to go through their wallets is not acceptable.)[/italic] -- Avoid killing players without prior roleplay or justified reasons. This is exempt if the Person engaged initiates before you do, or does not make an attempt to preserve themselves [italic](i.e. reacting to a gun being pointed to their head)[/italic] - [bold]You should not be killing people in such a way that will result in Round Removal (RR)[/bold], unless given as an Outlaw Job by another player's Character settings. - [bold]Act like a rebel[/bold]. Whilst you are not expected to act antagonistic at all times, it is still encouraged to act as an antagonist throughout the round whilst roleplaying. If your intentions aren’t to play an antagonist, play non-Outlaw role. - [bold]Other Outlaws are not necessarily your friends[/bold]. There may be honour amongst thieves, but they are not defaulting to your allies. You can betray other Outlaws, but you cannot betray Perdition. - [bold]You are required to have a good understanding of Outlaw GO-RP[/bold], or to be in the process of learning it. If you violate or fail to follow these documents, it is appropriate so long as you are making an effort to roleplay the consequences of these actions and still acting in ‘good faith’ for storytelling purposes.
## Theft/Robbing Players Theft should be a tool used, but not abused. Do not excessively take from players that you are stealing from in the below manners: - Do not engage in interactions that include stealing from someone's bank accounts. - If a player surrenders, keep plundering to a reasonable level such as not to ruin the player's round. - If they fight back, and you succeed, you are free to loot as you wish, but do not loot the ship in such a manner as to remove its ability to sustain life or fly. - We understand that during combat systems / walls can get damaged, you do not need to repair this, but leave enough materials for ships repairs.
If you are concerned that anything you’re about to do is may not be allowed, please aHelp and ask for clarification.
